gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada stands tall in its lowercase, with c, s and z drawn full and every curve ending in a clear opening. Capture It sits above it nearly sealed shut, a towering display face with barely a gap anywhere, so the two feel like opposites.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-radio-canada-bi: Radio Canada Big fills the line with a monoline skeleton and terminals that stop well clear of the stem. Capture It, urban and commanding, packs its letters nearly shut above that, so the plain sans below feels like a deep breath.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-readex-pro: Capture It is urban and commanding, with a towering x-height and openings so slight its letters look nearly sealed. Readex Pro runs the other way, with broad gaps at the terminals and a weight that holds steady word after word, so a long passage keeps moving.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-roboto: Commanding and urban, Capture It has no calligraphic swelling anywhere in its outlines, and its letters close up tight. Roboto gives round letters generous mouths and keeps capitals close to body height, so a long passage feels open after that heading.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-ruda: Approachable is the first word for Ruda, a wire-like monoline sans-serif with wide-mouthed rounds and a sizable x-height. Ruda against the sealed, towering Capture It gives the pair its best quality: one side shut tight, the other wide open.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-saira: Capture It is a towering, commanding display face with arches that match their stems. Saira follows in a lighter mood, with see-through s shapes and rounded letters stretching toward the top line, so the two feel like different speeds.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch keeps a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e and a compact gap up to the ascender line. Under Capture It, with its nearly sealed letters and hard, uniform strokes, a long page feels loose.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-savate: Capture It towers in its x-height, with letters nearly sealed and no swelling anywhere, which is where it earns its keep when big and short. Savate, a sans-serif, stays open on every curve.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-schibsted-grote: Nearly sealed letters and a towering x-height give Capture It its hard edge. Schibsted Grotesk has big, open-looking e and a shapes with tall bowls and terminals that never close in, so a long passage reads easily.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-sen: Capture It brings an urban, commanding weight, with a towering x-height and letters that sit nearly shut. And Sen, a modern sans-serif built tall with constant weight, lets its curves end before they turn inward, which opens the page up.
